text:
maya: Heads-up — starting a targeted stability probe for driver v555.12 + firmware 2.8. Plan: 50-node sample in eu-west1, 24h burn-in. Synthetic load + shadow of production. Goal: measure Xid frequency, ECC corrected/unrec counts, and any microreboots.

aj: SGTM. What are the hard thresholds for automatic rollback? need clear pass/fail criteria.

maya: Fail if sustained Xid rate > 3x baseline (baseline = last 7d avg per-node) OR ECC corrected increases by >0.2% absolute OR any uncorrectable ECC. Also rollback if GPU temp p90 shifts >4C vs baseline. If ambiguous, escalate for manual review.

opsbot: opsbot: probe scheduled: probe-id=probe-20260703-01 nodes=50 region=eu-west1 window=24h cohorts=5

sam: Quick reminder: previous candidate spike showed microreboots on kernel 6.5.9 after ~6h. Are we pinning kernel for this probe?

maya: Yes — kernel pinned to 6.4.11 for all probe nodes. Driver only change. Also enabling verbose NVML logging: `export NVML_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` and systemd unit to capture dmesg + nvml stack traces.

aj: Rollout policy? drain + replace pods in small batches, right? how many at a time?

maya: Rolling cohorts of 5 nodes. Drain procedure: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then cordon. Evacuate lower-priority batch workloads first. We'll tag reserve nodes with label `gpu:probe=false` to keep baseline capacity.

linda: Can we add a KV-cache perf smoke? In the past batching changes + firmware caused higher KV misses under certain kernels, which amplified load.

maya: Good call — add a smoke that runs a 10k-token cold KV pass then a warm KV pass to measure tokens/sec and KV hit ratio. Capture both latency and p50/p95 tails.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary artifacts pushed to eu-west1, probe start timestamp 2026-07-03T09:12:01Z

sam: If we observe an Xid spike but ECC unchanged, do we auto-rollback? sometimes Xid goes up during noisy-neighbor bursts.

maya: We treat an isolated, transient Xid bump differently: require sustained Xid >3x baseline for >30m AND correlation with driver stack traces referencing `nvidia-mig` / `nvlink` for auto-rollback. If it's noisy-neighbor only, flag for extended observation and increase sampling window.

aj: Cost note — 50 nodes * 24h ~= 1200 GPU-hours. Finance sign-off needed.

finance-team: finance-team: confirmed we can cover up to 1500 GPU-hours for this fiscal window; please paste final probe-id when done.

opsbot: opsbot: probe completed: probe-id=probe-20260703-01 status=completed duration=24h Xid_rate=0.9x_baseline ECC_corr=+0.05% temp_shift_p90=+1.1C anomalies=2 (microreboot traces)

maya: Initial read: overall Xid stayed below rollback threshold, ECC delta small. We did see microreboots on 2 nodes around hours 6-7. Uploading logs to `/mnt/probe-logs/probe-20260703-01.tar.gz` and nvml traces to the same bucket.

sam: Pulled one affected node, ran memtest and vendor diag — no UCEs. Suspect flaky card/secondary power cycling. Recommend evacuation + replace 2 cards rather than whole node reprovision.

maya: Agree. Action: mark nodes as `gpu:needs-replace`, schedule hardware swap in the next maintenance window, and file a vendor RMA with serials attached.

aj: :thumbsup: can we include per-card power draw and rail noise plots in the ticket? want to check for power instability patterns.

linda: I'll correlate telemetry from `/telemetry/pci/power` and upload plots to the ticket.

opsbot: opsbot: maintenance ticket created: MNT-4872 linked to probe-20260703-01
